danishChanges.before: Før du angriber en hær, belejrer en fæstning eller dræber en bestemt person, så find ud af navnene på den ansvarlige general, hans nærmeste medhjælpere, dem der fører besøgende ind i Audiensen, portneren og vagterne på post. danishChanges.after: Vil du angribe en hær, belejre en fæstning eller dræbe en bestemt person, skal du først kende navnene på den ansvarlige feltherre, hans nærmeste mænd, dem, der fører besøgende ind til ham, portvagten og vagtposterne. Sæt derefter spioner til at holde øje med dem.
danishChanges.reason: Modern idiomatic Danish and source fidelity; remove false envy, divine Lord, flood-as-river and wooden espionage labels.

danishChanges.before: Find de fjendtlige agenter, der er sendt for at holde øje med os. Betal dem, sørg for husly og pleje til dem, og bring dem i vores tjeneste. De sætter os i stand til at hverve flere agenter blandt modstanderens landsbyboere og embedsmænd.
danishChanges.after: Opspor fjendens spioner, der kommer for at udspionere os. Giv dem penge, sørg for deres ophold og pleje, og få dem over i vores tjeneste. Gennem dem kan vi hverve spioner blandt fjendens landsbyboere og embedsmænd.
danishChanges.reason: Modern idiomatic Danish and source fidelity; remove false envy, divine Lord, flood-as-river and wooden espionage labels.

danishChanges.before: En agent, der er vundet over fra modstanderen, sætter os i stand til at finde på en opdigtet beretning, som en dødsspion kan tage med tilbage til ham.
danishChanges.after: Gennem dobbeltagenten kan vi udforme en falsk historie, som dødsspionen skal bringe til fjenden.
danishChanges.reason: Modern idiomatic Danish and source fidelity; remove false envy, divine Lord, flood-as-river and wooden espionage labels.

danishChanges.before: Den omvendte agent sætter os i stand til at bruge alle fem slags spioner til størst mulig gavn. Han må derfor behandles rundhåndet.
danishChanges.after: Dobbeltagenten gør det muligt at bruge alle fem slags spioner med størst fordel. Derfor skal han behandles gavmildt.
danishChanges.reason: Modern idiomatic Danish and source fidelity; remove false envy, divine Lord, flood-as-river and wooden espionage labels.

danishChanges.before: Kloge fyrster og tænksomme generaler vælger derfor de mest intelligente mænd til spionage og opnår stadig stor anseelse. En hær kan ikke undvære sin spion: selve dens bevægelser afhænger af ham.
danishChanges.after: Derfor bruger intelligente fyrster og kloge feltherrer de dygtigste mænd som spioner og udmærker sig altid. Spionen er uundværlig for hæren. Dens bevægelser afhænger af ham.
danishChanges.reason: Modern idiomatic Danish and source fidelity; remove false envy, divine Lord, flood-as-river and wooden espionage labels.

englishChanges.before: A commander serving me who follows my plans in battle wins consistently, and I keep him in my service. One who departs from those plans will lose and be removed from his command.
englishChanges.after: A commander serving me who follows my plans in battle always wins, and I keep him in my service. One who departs from those plans will lose and be removed from his command.
englishChanges.reason: Preserve source absolute always.

englishChanges.before: The finest soldier therefore defeats his opponent's thinking with a better plan. Next comes the one who stops hostile forces from joining together; after him, the one who fights their army. Laying siege to their stronghold is the least desirable course.
englishChanges.after: The most skilful warrior therefore outwits his opponent with a better strategy. Next comes the one who stops hostile forces from joining together; after him, the one who fights their army. Laying siege to their stronghold is the least desirable course.
englishChanges.reason: Restore source sense and remove awkward or misleading rendering.

englishChanges.before: The rules of warfare prescribe encirclement when your strength is tenfold the enemy's, an attack when it is fivefold, and division when your numbers are double. With equal strength, fight with every effort. With fewer men, manoeuvre until an opening comes. If overwhelmingly inferior, give no opportunity for battle. Stubborn resistance by a smaller force only results in its being taken prisoner.
englishChanges.after: The rules of warfare prescribe encirclement when your strength is tenfold the enemy's, an attack when it is fivefold, and division when your numbers are double. With equal strength, fight with every effort. With fewer men, manoeuvre until an opening comes. If inferior in every respect, give no opportunity for battle. Stubborn resistance by a smaller force only results in its being taken prisoner.
englishChanges.reason: Restore source sense and remove awkward or misleading rendering.

englishChanges.before: This plants suspicion in the minds of the troops.
englishChanges.after: This fills the troops with distrust.
englishChanges.reason: Restore source sense and remove awkward or misleading rendering.

englishChanges.before: When bewilderment and suspicion possess an army, neighbouring rulers become a threat. The troops are thrown into confusion and delivered into their opponent's hands.
englishChanges.after: When bewilderment and distrust possess an army, neighbouring rulers become a threat. The troops are thrown into confusion and delivered into their opponent's hands.
englishChanges.reason: Restore source sense and remove awkward or misleading rendering.

englishChanges.before: An old teaching says that understanding both sides removes fear even through a hundred encounters. Someone who ignores his opponent and attends only to himself wins once and loses the next time. Someone ignorant both of his opponent and of the resources he himself possesses loses every time.
englishChanges.after: An old teaching says that understanding both sides removes fear even through a hundred encounters. Someone who does not know his opponent and attends only to himself wins once and loses the next time. Someone ignorant both of his opponent and of the resources he himself possesses loses every time.
englishChanges.reason: Restore source sense and remove awkward or misleading rendering.

englishChanges.before: An old saying teaches that the accomplished soldier wins without desperate, blood-soaked encounters, and consequently gains no fame for cleverness or heroism. For him, entering battle means winning it: he attacks only after his opponent has already created the causes of his own defeat.
englishChanges.after: An old saying teaches that the accomplished soldier wins without desperate, blood-soaked encounters, and consequently gains no fame for wisdom or brave deeds. For him, entering battle means winning it: he attacks only after his opponent has already created the causes of his own defeat.
englishChanges.reason: Modern idiom; consistent military morale terminology; clarify surveying instrument, restore source imagery and avoid literal English calques.

englishChanges.before: The principles of warfare are said to proceed through five stages: the rule, the measure, the tables, the scales, and finally the prediction of success.
englishChanges.after: The principles of warfare are said to proceed through five stages: the measuring rule, the measure, the tables, the scales, and finally the prediction of success.
englishChanges.reason: Modern idiom; consistent military morale terminology; clarify surveying instrument, restore source imagery and avoid literal English calques.

englishChanges.before: The rule surveys the territory; the measure establishes how much it produces; the tables record its inhabitants; the scales reveal their weight or quality. From this we can then work out whether the result will be success or failure.
englishChanges.after: The measuring rule surveys the territory; the measure establishes how much it produces; the tables record its inhabitants; the scales reveal their weight or quality. From this we can then work out whether the result will be success or failure.
englishChanges.reason: Modern idiom; consistent military morale terminology; clarify surveying instrument, restore source imagery and avoid literal English calques.

englishChanges.before: Suppose we wish for battle, but the opponent rests content behind tall walls and broad, deep moats. We then strike at another place whose relief will force him to emerge.
englishChanges.after: Suppose we wish for battle, but the opponent rests content behind tall walls and deep moats. We then strike at another place whose relief will force him to emerge.
englishChanges.reason: Remove invented details and preserve source prohibition and modality.

englishChanges.before: If our opponent has many men, stop him exploiting that advantage and find out his campaign plan. Stir him into action to learn the condition of his troops; make a feint to test his position's strength. Spread and beat your wings to reveal whether his resources are adequate. Repeated feints and forays can make us seem impossible to grasp, an impression that neither spying nor cleverness can remove.
englishChanges.after: If our opponent has many men, stop him exploiting that advantage and find out his campaign plan. Stir him into action to learn the condition of his troops; make a feint to test his position's strength. Beat your wings to reveal whether his resources are adequate. Repeated feints and forays can make us seem impossible to grasp, an impression that neither spying nor cleverness can remove.
englishChanges.reason: Remove invented details and preserve source prohibition and modality.

englishChanges.before: Do not use a plan again merely because it once brought success. Change your methods as circumstances change.
englishChanges.after: If a strategy has brought victory, do not repeat it. Change your methods as circumstances change.
englishChanges.reason: Remove invented details and preserve source prohibition and modality.

englishChanges.before: An army can be compared with flowing water.
englishChanges.after: An army can be compared with water.
englishChanges.reason: Remove invented details and preserve source prohibition and modality.

englishChanges.before: A commander who adapts his methods to his opponent and thus determines the outcome deserves the name God of war.
englishChanges.after: A commander who adapts his methods to his opponent and thus determines the outcome may be called the God of war.
englishChanges.reason: Remove invented details and preserve source prohibition and modality.

englishChanges.before: An army's actions can bring benefits; the quarrelling of an unruly crowd carries grave dangers.
englishChanges.after: An army's actions can bring benefits; the quarrelling of a crowd carries grave dangers.
englishChanges.reason: Retain source distinctions and remove unsupported qualifier.

englishChanges.before: Once everyone acts together, brave men cannot press ahead on their own, nor can frightened men fall back without restraint. This is how a large body of men can be employed.
englishChanges.after: Once everyone acts together, strong men cannot press ahead on their own, nor can frightened men fall back without restraint. This is how a large body of men can be employed.
englishChanges.reason: Retain source distinctions and remove unsupported qualifier.

englishChanges.before: Preserve strength by waiting for an opponent travelling from far away, meeting his hunger with your own fullness, and bringing fatigue against rest.
englishChanges.after: Preserve strength by waiting for an opponent travelling from far away, meeting his hunger with your own fullness, and facing his fatigue with your own rest.
englishChanges.reason: Explicit editorial emendation: Calthrop reverses rest and fatigue. Giles VII.31 supports rested troops facing a tired enemy; source retained unchanged, variant to be disclosed in reading notes.

englishChanges.before: When directing armies, if you understand the practice of the Nine Changes, knowing the Five Advantages is of no use.
englishChanges.after: When directing armies, knowing the Five Advantages is of no use if you do not understand the practice of the Nine Changes.
englishChanges.reason: Explicit editorial emendation: Calthrop's 'be understood' appears to omit a negative. Giles VIII.6 supports 'do not understand'; existing Danish already follows this reading. Disclose in reading notes; original unchanged.

englishChanges.before: Care for the men's health and place their camp on elevated, sunlit ground: this will keep sickness away and ensure a successful outcome.
englishChanges.after: Care for the troops' health and camp on high, sunny ground: this will prevent disease and ensure victory.
englishChanges.reason: Restore source meaning: victory, smooth rather than merely pleasant speech, and always rather than consistently.

englishChanges.before: Pleasant talk combined with energetic preparations indicates that the opposing force intends to move forward and attack.
englishChanges.after: Busy preparations and smooth words show that the enemy is about to advance to attack.
englishChanges.reason: Restore source meaning: victory, smooth rather than merely pleasant speech, and always rather than consistently.

englishChanges.before: Where commander and men understand one another, instructions are consistently carried out.
englishChanges.after: When commander and soldiers understand one another, orders are always obeyed.
englishChanges.reason: Restore source meaning: victory, smooth rather than merely pleasant speech, and always rather than consistently.

englishChanges.before: Terrain serves as an attendant to success.
englishChanges.after: Terrain helps bring victory.
englishChanges.reason: Remove wooden attendant-to-success calque while preserving terrain's supporting role.

englishChanges.before: The accomplished fighters of earlier times took care to sever their opponent's front from his rear. They separated his small detachments from his larger forces, stopped officers and men from helping one another, and sowed suspicion between higher and lower ranks. They dispersed his troops and kept them from gathering together; even when assembled, those troops lacked a common purpose.
englishChanges.after: The accomplished fighters of earlier times took care to sever their opponent's front from his rear. They separated his small detachments from his larger forces, stopped officers and men from helping one another, and spread distrust between higher and lower ranks. They dispersed his troops and kept them from gathering together; even when assembled, those troops lacked unity.
englishChanges.reason: Repair source meaning and strained English: unity, distrust, attack an unprepared force, proof against defeat, retrieval from danger.

englishChanges.before: More than anything else in war, rapid action keeps the troops' spirit alive. Strike before your opponent has prepared; come upon his unreadiness from a direction he does not anticipate.
englishChanges.after: Above all in war, speed sustains the troops' spirit. Strike before the enemy is ready, attacking his unprepared force from an unexpected direction.
englishChanges.reason: Repair source meaning and strained English: unity, distrust, attack an unprepared force, proof against defeat, retrieval from danger.

englishChanges.before: Consider warfare abroad. Troops who are strangers in a distant land stand together and withstand defeat. Raid productive plains to feed the army. Look after the men's health, avoid wearing them out needlessly, bring their minds together, accumulate strength, and plan carefully in secret. When they have nowhere to find shelter, the men will not run from death.
englishChanges.after: Consider warfare abroad. Troops who are strangers in a distant land stand together and cannot be defeated. Raid productive plains to feed the army. Look after the men's health, avoid wearing them out needlessly, bring their minds together, accumulate strength, and plan carefully in secret. When they have nowhere to find shelter, the men will not run from death.
englishChanges.reason: Repair source meaning and strained English: unity, distrust, attack an unprepared force, proof against defeat, retrieval from danger.

englishChanges.before: Throw troops into peril and they survive; put them on death ground and they can recover. It is the force facing danger that wins.
englishChanges.after: Throw troops into danger and they survive; on death ground they can find a way out. It is the force facing danger that wins.
englishChanges.reason: Repair source meaning and strained English: unity, distrust, attack an unprepared force, proof against defeat, retrieval from danger.

englishChanges.before: For water to support an assault, its flood must sweep everything before it.
englishChanges.after: For water to support an attack, the flood must be overwhelming.
englishChanges.reason: Clarify source meaning without adding claims; ruler not deity, power not merely influence, presence as commander's audience, retain absolute invariably.

englishChanges.before: Use all five methods together and no one can trace how they operate. Their name is the Mysterious Thread, and they are the Lord's Treasure.
englishChanges.after: Use all five methods at once, and no one can discover how they work. This is called the Mysterious Thread: it is the ruler's treasure.
englishChanges.reason: Clarify source meaning without adding claims; ruler not deity, power not merely influence, presence as commander's audience, retain absolute invariably.

englishChanges.before: The influence that spies possess is truly remarkable.
englishChanges.after: The power of spies is truly remarkable.
englishChanges.reason: Clarify source meaning without adding claims; ruler not deity, power not merely influence, presence as commander's audience, retain absolute invariably.

englishChanges.before: Before assaulting an army, besieging a stronghold, or killing a particular individual, learn the names of the commander responsible, his closest assistants, the people who bring visitors into the Presence, the gatekeeper, and the guards on watch. englishChanges.after: Before attacking an army, besieging a fortress, or killing a particular person, learn the names of the commander in charge, his closest assistants, those who bring visitors before him, the gatekeeper, and the sentries. Then have your spies watch them.
englishChanges.reason: Clarify source meaning without adding claims; ruler not deity, power not merely influence, presence as commander's audience, retain absolute invariably.

englishChanges.before: Discerning rulers and thoughtful commanders consequently select the most intelligent men for spying and consistently achieve great distinction. An army cannot do without its spy: its very movements depend upon him.
englishChanges.after: Discerning rulers and thoughtful commanders consequently select the most intelligent men for spying and invariably achieve great distinction. An army cannot do without its spy: its very movements depend upon him.
